title: Simple Coding
source: MindSpark Grade 4 Aptitude & Reasoning | Chapter 5: Simple Coding
subtopics: Word coding — encode a word using the rule
Decode a coded message back to the original
learningGoals: Apply a letter-shift rule to encode and decode simple words.
Use a number code (A=1, B=2...) to encode and decode short words.
Spot the coding rule from one given example and apply it to a new word.
coreIdeas: A code replaces each letter with a different letter, number, or symbol using a fixed rule.
To crack a code: find what rule changes A to the coded letter, then apply that same rule to every letter.
Encoding means hiding the message; decoding means finding the original message.

workedExamples.problem: In a code, A is written as B, B as C, C as D. How is CAT written in this code?
workedExamples.solution: Each letter shifts +1 forward. C→D, A→B, T→U. So CAT is coded as DBU.

workedExamples.problem: In a code, A=1, B=2, C=3 ... Z=26. How is DOG written in numbers?
workedExamples.solution: D=4, O=15, G=7. So DOG is coded as 4-15-7.

workedExamples.problem: In a code, A is written as Z, B as Y, C as X (reverse alphabet). How is CAT written?
workedExamples.solution: C→X, A→Z, T→G. So CAT is coded as XZG.

onboarding.coachIntro: Spark the coach opens Simple Coding by pretending to send a secret message: 'BFF = AGG if we shift each letter back by one!' This instantly sparks curiosity. Spark then explains the encode/decode concept and the three types of codes before the first exercise.
onboarding.placementRule: Start at Group A for all learners. If two consecutive wrong answers in Groups A–B, slow down and work letter-by-letter using the alphabet strip before continuing.

mission.missionPromise: By the end, you will encode and decode secret messages using shift codes, number codes, and reverse codes — just like a real spy!
mission.successCelebration: Award a badge pulse and coach cheer after every correct group. At lesson end, show 'Code Breaker' trophy.

microLessonPattern: Coach opens with a spy-themed hook.
Coach shows a worked encode/decode example step by step.
Coach reads the practice question with the code rule stated clearly.
Student applies the rule to encode or decode the word.
Instant feedback shows the letter-by-letter working.
Review question confirms mastery before next group.

rewardLoop.xpUnit: Award 10 to 22 XP per exercise group.
rewardLoop.streakRule: Show streak counter; protect with one free retry before streak breaks.

rewardLoop.celebrationStyle: Quick coach praise + XP pulse + progress rail tick after every correct answer.

beats.teacherLine: Hello, secret agent! Welcome to Simple Coding — where you learn to write and crack secret messages! Spies use codes all the time. A code takes each letter of a word and changes it using a special rule. If you know the rule, you can encode any message and decode any mystery! Today we will learn three cool codes: the shift code, the number code, and the reverse alphabet code. Ready to go undercover?
beats.boardAction: Write 'Simple Coding' as the title. Below, list the three codes: (1) Shift code — move each letter forward or backward, (2) Number code — A=1, B=2..., (3) Reverse code — A=Z, B=Y...
beats.checkpointPrompt: Quick warm-up: if A is written as B and B is written as C, what letter does D become?
beats.expectedStudentResponse: E — each letter moves one step forward.
beats.fallbackHint: The rule is: add 1 to the letter's position. D is the 4th letter; 4+1=5; the 5th letter is E!

beats.teacherLine: Let me encode a word using the +1 shift code! I want to encode the word CAT. Rule: each letter moves one step forward in the alphabet. C is the 3rd letter — one step forward is D. A is the 1st — one step forward is B. T is the 20th — one step forward is U. So CAT becomes DBU. To decode DBU, I just reverse the rule — move each letter one step BACK: D→C, B→A, U→T. That gives me back CAT!
beats.boardAction: Write C → D, A → B, T → U on the board side by side. Circle DBU as the coded word. Below, show decoding: D → C, B → A, U → T → CAT.
beats.checkpointPrompt: Your turn: encode the word SUN using the +1 shift code.
beats.fallbackHint: S is the 19th letter; 19+1=20=T. U is 21st; 21+1=22=V. N is 14th; 14+1=15=O. SUN = TVO.

svgAnimation.text: CAT is coded as: D B U

beats.teacherLine: You have all three code types — shift, number, and reverse. Now it is time to put on your spy hat! Work through Groups A to G. For every question, first write down the rule, then apply it letter by letter. Never rush — secret agents are careful and accurate!
beats.boardAction: Write alphabet strip A=1 through Z=26 for reference. Show reverse code pairs: A-Z, B-Y, C-X, D-W, E-V, F-U, G-T, H-S, I-R, J-Q, K-P, L-O, M-N.
beats.checkpointPrompt: Quick check: in the number code A=1, B=2 ... what is the number for the letter M?
beats.fallbackHint: Count the alphabet: A=1, B=2, C=3 ... J=10, K=11, L=12, M=13. M is number 13!

sessionFlow.missionStepTitle: Exercise A: Shift Each Letter Forward
sessionFlow.coachHook: Let's figure this out together! Move every letter one step forward in the alphabet. A→B, B→C, C→D ...

boardDemo.title: +1 Shift Code — Encode
boardDemo.teacherLine: Write the alphabet positions under each letter. Add 1 to each position. Write the new letter above. That is your coded word!

sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: Using the +1 shift code, what does the word RUN become when encoded?
sessionFlow.tryPrompt: Now you try: encode the word CAP using the +1 shift rule.
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Spot on! C→D, A→B, P→Q. CAP becomes DBQ. Secret agent approved!
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: Here's a trick: write the position of each letter — C=3, A=1, P=16. Add 1: 4, 2, 17. Convert back: D, B, Q. So CAP = DBQ.
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: Quick: encode the word HAT using the +1 shift rule.

sessionFlow.missionStepTitle: Exercise B: Decode the Shift Message
sessionFlow.coachHook: Let's figure this out together! To decode a +1 shift message, reverse the rule — move every letter one step BACK.

boardDemo.title: +1 Shift Code — Decode
steps: Rule to decode: move each letter -1 back
Wait — let us check: EOX does not make a word. Try: F→E, P→O, Y→X. EOX. Sometimes coded words do not spell real words — that is the secret!
boardDemo.teacherLine: Decoding is just encoding in reverse. If the rule was +1, to decode you do -1. Move every letter one step BACK in the alphabet.

sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: A secret message says TVO. If the code was +1 shift, what is the original word?
sessionFlow.tryPrompt: Your turn: decode the message IFM using the +1 shift code (move each letter back by 1).
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Great decoding! I(9)→H(8), F(6)→E(5), M(13)→L(12). IFM decoded = HEL. Mission accomplished!
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: Here's a trick: coding was +1, so decoding is −1. I is the 9th letter, minus 1 = 8th = H. F is 6th, minus 1 = 5th = E. M is 13th, minus 1 = 12th = L.
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: Quick: decode DBQ using the +1 shift code.

sessionFlow.coachHook: Let's figure this out together! Every letter has a number — A=1, B=2 right up to Z=26. Turn the word into a number sequence!

boardDemo.title: Number Code — A=1, B=2 ...
steps: To decode: replace each number with its letter (count to that position)
boardDemo.teacherLine: The number code is like turning every letter into its position in the alphabet. S is the 19th letter, so S=19. Decode by counting to that position in the alphabet.

sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: What is the number code for the word CAT? (A=1, B=2 ... C=3, T=20)
sessionFlow.tryPrompt: Your turn: encode the word DOG using the number code (D=4, O=15, G=7).
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Yes! D=4, O=15, G=7. DOG becomes 4-15-7. You cracked the number code!
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: Here's a trick: count D in the alphabet — A=1, B=2, C=3, D=4. Count O: that is the 15th letter. G is the 7th. So DOG = 4-15-7.
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: Quick: decode 2-9-7 using the number code (A=1, B=2 ...).

sessionFlow.coachHook: Let's figure this out together! In the reverse code, A becomes Z and Z becomes A — the alphabet is flipped upside down!

boardDemo.title: Reverse Code — Mirror the Alphabet
steps: Rule: add the position + reverse position = 27 always!
boardDemo.teacherLine: Magic trick: to find the reverse code of any letter, subtract its position from 27. C=3, 27−3=24=X. A=1, 27−1=26=Z. T=20, 27−20=7=G.

sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: In the reverse code, what does the letter M (position 13) become? (Hint: 27 − 13 = ?)
sessionFlow.tryPrompt: Your turn: encode the word BIG using the reverse code (27 minus position of each letter).
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Brilliant! B=2 → 27-2=25=Y. I=9 → 27-9=18=R. G=7 → 27-7=20=T. BIG = YRT. Reverse code mastered!
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: Here's a trick: use the magic formula 27 − position = reverse. B is position 2: 27−2=25, the 25th letter is Y. I is position 9: 27−9=18=R. G is 7: 27−7=20=T.
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: Quick: decode YRT back to the original word using the reverse code.

sessionFlow.subtopic: Spot the coding rule from one example
sessionFlow.missionStepTitle: Exercise E: Find the Code Rule
sessionFlow.coachHook: Let's figure this out together! You are given one coded example. Use it to figure out the secret rule — then apply it to a new word!

boardDemo.title: Crack the Rule from One Clue
steps: Given: if CAT is coded as DBU
Rule found: +1 shift. Now apply to any new word!
boardDemo.teacherLine: To find the rule, compare the original letter with the coded letter. Find what number was added or subtracted to the position. Confirm with a second letter. Once confirmed, apply the same rule to the new word.

sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: If DOG is coded as EPH, what is the rule? (D=4, E=5; O=15, P=16; G=7, H=8)
sessionFlow.tryPrompt: Given that CAT = DBU, how would you write the word SUN in the same code?
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: You got it! Rule = +1 shift. S→T, U→V, N→O. SUN = TVO. Rule-spotting champion!
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: Here's a trick: C→D is +1. Use that rule on every letter of SUN. S is 19, add 1 = 20 = T. U is 21, add 1 = 22 = V. N is 14, add 1 = 15 = O.
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: Quick: if A is coded as C, B as D, C as E — what is the code rule and what does the word BIG become?

sessionFlow.coachHook: Let's figure this out together! Sometimes letters are replaced by symbols — stars, circles, triangles. Crack the symbol table and decode the message!

boardDemo.title: Symbol Substitution Code
steps: Code table: A=★, B=●, C=▲, D=■, E=◆
Message: C A B  D E → CAB DE
boardDemo.teacherLine: A symbol code is the same as any other code — just look up the symbol in the code table to find the letter. Always decode one symbol at a time, left to right.

sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: Code table: A=1, E=2, I=3, O=4, U=5. What does the code '3 4 5' say?
sessionFlow.tryPrompt: Your turn: if ★=S, ●=U, ▲=N — what word does ★●▲ spell?
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: Here's a trick: use the code table like a dictionary. Look up each symbol one at a time. ★ = S, ● = U, ▲ = N. Put them together: SUN.
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: Create your own mini symbol code for 3 letters and encode a 3-letter word. Then ask a friend to decode it!

sessionFlow.subtopic: Decode a coded message back to the original
sessionFlow.missionStepTitle: Exercise G: Full Message Decode Challenge
sessionFlow.coachHook: Let's figure this out together — this is the big mission! A full coded sentence is waiting. Find the rule, decode every word, and reveal the secret message!

boardDemo.title: Full Decode — Step by Step
steps: Decode each letter: I→H, F→E, M→L, M→L, P→O
Decoded: H E L L O
Always apply the decode rule (reverse of encode rule) to every letter
boardDemo.teacherLine: Decode word by word, letter by letter. Write the decode rule at the top of your working area. Then go through every letter patiently. Accuracy beats speed here!

sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: Using the +1 shift decode (move each letter back by 1), what does XPSME mean?
sessionFlow.tryPrompt: Final challenge: decode the message 23-15-18-12-4 using the number code (A=1, B=2 ...).
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: AMAZING! 23=W, 15=O, 18=R, 12=L, 4=D. The message says WORLD. You decoded a full message like a true spy!
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: Here's a trick: convert each number to its alphabet position. 23=W (count to 23rd letter), 15=O, 18=R, 12=L, 4=D. Put them together: WORLD.
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: Final review: encode the word STAR using the +1 shift code, then swap with a classmate to decode!
